getting-started.title: 🚀 Getting started

sections.text: Asking for a motion in a scene

getting-started.text: 🚀 Getting started The folders it needs The plugin is developed next to the projects it uses: go.mod replaces Go Simulator and Go Renderer with the folders beside this one. Clone them side by side: go-renderer/ go-simulator/ go-simulator-motion/ ← this repository Running the example cd ../go-simulator go run ./cmd/simulator -rules ../go-simulator-motion/examples/living-scene.yaml scene.glb scene.glb is any glTF 2.0 scene. The viewer shows it while the plugin moves it. examples/living-scene.yaml starts the plugin with go run from this repository, so it needs no installing. After go install github.com/akrck02/go-simulator-motion@latest the command can be just [go-simulator-motion] . plugins: - name: motion command: [go, run, .] directory: .. stages: - name: motion clock: realtime rules: - rule: day_cycle with: {seconds_per_day: 120} enabled: false toggle_key: T - rule: gusts with: {variation: 0.5, veering: 0.35} - rule: cloud_drift - rule: tides with: {seconds_per_day: 120} toggle_key: M - rule: entity_motion All the rules sit in one stage on a realtime clock, so they follow the viewer's clock. The day cycle starts switched off; the rules file's reference explains every key. The keys Key What it does T Turns the day cycle on and off ( toggle_key in the example) M Turns the tides off and on ( toggle_key in the example) P Pauses and resumes time , and . Halve or double the speed of time The viewer's own keys (moving the camera and so on) work as usual. Asking for a motion in a scene glTF node extras arrive as the entity's properties, so a scene asks for a motion without any code. A boat that bobs, sails that turn and a ferry on a loop, in a scene's nodes : { "name": "boat", "extras": { "bob": { "height": 0.5, "period": 4, "roll": 0.05 } } }, { "name": "sails", "extras": { "spin": { "axis": [0, 0, 1], "speed": 0.8 } } }, { "name": "ferry", "extras": { "path": { "points": [[-30, 0, -30], [30, 0, -30], [30, 0, 30], [-30, 0, 30]], "speed": 4, "loop": true } } } Every key and what it is when left out are in motions . Entities that other plugins add later with these properties start moving too. The tests go vet ./... go test ./... The tests run the plugin inside a Go Simulator host and check that the sun turns, the clouds drift with the wind, the tide turns and can be switched off, the wind gusts within its range, that a path goes there and back, and that bob wins over spin.

how-it-works.title: 🔍 How it works

sections.text: How the plugin fits Go Simulator
How the rules are stepped over time

how-it-works.text: 🔍 How it works How the plugin fits Go Simulator Go Simulator is the host. It loads the scene, keeps the world (its entities and its environment) and moves the clock. The motion plugin is a separate program the host starts; they talk over standard input and output (Go Simulator's protocol ). At the start the plugin describes itself: its five rules, their parameters, what each one reads and what it writes. That description is also where the rules reference comes from. The four environment rules read the environment and write environment : the sun direction, the wind, the clouds' offset and the tide angle. entity_motion reads only the entities with a bob , spin or path property and writes transforms . A plugin never touches the renderer: it reads its copy of the world and answers with changes (Go Simulator's writing plugins ). The renderer then draws the sky, the sway of plants, the clouds and the water from the environment, and the entities where their transforms put them. Shapes are in world units and fields in physical units, as Go Simulator's vocabulary lists. How the rules are stepped over time The example's rules are on a realtime clock. Every frame the viewer advances that stage by the seconds that passed, times the speed: Each switched-on rule gets one step : the host sends the stage time and the step in seconds, the rule reads its copy of the world and answers with changes. The host applies them and forwards them to any other plugin that reads them. Pause ( P ) sends no steps; the motions stop where they are. Speed ( , . ) makes the steps shorter or longer, so everything moves slower or faster together. A toggle key turns its rule off or on. A rule that is off is not stepped at all: the tide stays at its angle, and the day cycle in the example waits for T . The rules work in rates, not frames: the sun turns 2π × step / seconds_per_day , the tide 2π × step / period , a path moves speed × step . So a slow and a fast computer show the same scene after the same time. gusts and entity_motion keep their own count of the seconds they have been stepped, so a rule switched off and on again picks up where it stopped. How the pictures were made The pictures in these pages that show motion (the bay at the top of the README, the strips, the sky and the clouds, and the three entity panels) were drawn from the plugin's own answers. A small throwaway program, kept outside the repository, ran the real plugin in a Go Simulator host with examples/living-scene.yaml , switched the day cycle on with T as the viewer would, put a made-up bay in the world (a ferry on a looping path, a skiff on one that goes out and back, two buoys that bob, a mill that spins), advanced the clock 0.1 seconds at a time for two minutes, and drew where everything was. They are SVG drawings with their own light and dark colours, not screenshots of the viewer: the repository has no example scene whose entities ask for a motion, and the look of the sky and the water is the renderer's work, not this plugin's. The diagrams (how it fits, the two kinds of motion, the steps over time) were drawn by hand in the same style.

overview.title: Welcome to Go Motion Simulator 👋

sections.text: All the pages, in reading order

overview.text: Welcome to Go Motion Simulator 👋 The motion plugin makes a scene feel alive : the sun crosses the sky, the wind gusts, clouds drift, the tide rises, boats bob and sails turn. It works while you watch: it moves the sun, the wind, the clouds and the tide, and anything in the scene that asks to move ( bob , spin , or follow a path ). Is it for me? ✅ You use Go Simulator and want a scene that moves . ✅ You want to set it up by writing a rules file : no programming needed. ✅ You are curious about the science behind it: the pages explain the model with pictures. Where to start Pick the line that sounds like you. If you… Read Time are new and want to see it work 🏴‍☠️ The quest : a harbour that never keeps still, in 5 levels 45 min want to run its example Getting started 10 min want to know what each motion does The model 10 min are looking up a parameter Rules reference — All the pages, in reading order The menu on the left (or the files in docs/ ) follows this order. Start Overview : this page The quest Getting started Understand The model How it works Reference Rules reference 🚧 Not done yet Pictures of the 3D viewer itself. The repository has no example scene with entities that ask for a motion, so the pictures in these pages are 2D drawings of what the plugin answered, not screenshots (see how the pictures were made ). The heights and phases of the tide, the sway of plants and the look of day, twilight and night are worked out by the renderer from what this plugin writes; they are not shown here. An entity takes a single motion: a boat cannot both bob and follow a path. Words you will meet Word What it means Terminal The window where you type commands: Terminal on macOS and Linux, PowerShell on Windows. Repository A project's folder of files, kept on GitHub. git clone <address> copies it to your computer. Plugin A small program that adds one ability to another: here, one kind of simulation each. Rules file A text file (YAML) that says which plugins to use, with which numbers, for how long: no programming needed. Field A grid of numbers laid over the world: the height of every spot, its temperature, its rain. Quest The tutorial of these docs: short levels, each ending with something that works and an achievement. The family Go Motion Simulator is one of a family of small projects that work together: Project What it does Go Renderer draws 3D scenes and flat interfaces Go UI buttons, panels and whole applications Go UI for Android Android apps that look like Android's own Go Sound sound and music Go Scene Builder 3D scenes from a flat map Go Simulator simulations that change a scene Go Terrain Simulator ground shaped by rivers Go Climate Simulator weather and biomes Go Flora Simulator forests that grow Go Urban Simulator towns that grow Go Motion Simulator (this one) a scene that moves Go for 3DS Go on the Nintendo 3DS ⚠️ All of them are educational experiments , written with an AI assistant and pending review by their author: good for learning and playing, not for production.

rules-reference.title: 📏 Rules of the motion plugin
rules-reference.text: 📏 Rules of the motion plugin Version 1.0.0, protocol 2. Day cycle, wind gusts, drifting clouds, tides and the motions entities ask for (bob, spin, path). This reference is generated from what the plugin itself tells the host (the describe message), so it always matches the code. Parameters go under with: in a rules file; see Go Simulator's rules file reference . Rule What it does day_cycle Turns the sun around the celestial pole; the stars follow it. gusts Varies the wind strength and direction around the wind the world started with. cloud_drift Moves the clouds with the wind. tides Raises and lowers the water: turns the tide angle a full turn per period. Heights and phases come with the scene. entity_motion Moves the entities that ask for it in their properties: bob (float and roll), spin (turn on an axis) and path (follow points). day_cycle Turns the sun around the celestial pole; the stars follow it. Reads: the environment Writes: environment Parameter Type Default Meaning seconds_per_day number 120 how long a whole day lasts gusts Varies the wind strength and direction around the wind the world started with. Reads: the environment Writes: environment Parameter Type Default Meaning variation number 0.5 how much the strength changes (0..1) veering number 0.35 how far the direction swings, in radians cloud_drift Moves the clouds with the wind. Reads: the environment Writes: environment Parameter Type Default Meaning speed number 0.05 cloud-pattern units per second at wind strength 1 tides Raises and lowers the water: turns the tide angle a full turn per period. Heights and phases come with the scene. Reads: the environment Writes: environment Parameter Type Default Meaning period_seconds number 0 seconds per tidal cycle (0 = 12.42 h in proportion to seconds_per_day) seconds_per_day number 120 day length used when period_seconds is 0 entity_motion Moves the entities that ask for it in their properties: bob (float and roll), spin (turn on an axis) and path (follow points). Reads: entities with property bob , spin , path Writes: nothing of its own (it moves the entities that carry bob , spin or path ) No parameters.

the-model.title: 🌊 Motions
the-model.text: 🌊 Motions A still scene feels like a photograph. The motion plugin makes it feel alive: the sun crosses the sky, the wind picks up and dies down, clouds drift past, the sea rises and falls, boats bob and mill sails turn. It works in real time, while you watch the 3D scene. It changes the environment (sun, wind, clouds, tide) and the transforms of entities that ask for a motion. Its rules belong on a realtime clock; the speed keys of the viewer ( , . ) and the pause ( P ) apply to them. The environment Rule What it does day_cycle Turns the sun around the celestial pole once every seconds_per_day (120); the stars follow it, and the renderer derives day, twilight and night from the sun's height gusts Varies the wind's strength ( variation , 0.5) and direction ( veering , 0.35 rad) around the wind the world started with; plants marked to sway bend with it and clouds drift cloud_drift Moves the clouds with the wind ( speed , 0.05) tides Turns the tide angle a full turn per period ( period_seconds ; 0 = 12.42 h in proportion to seconds_per_day ). The tide's heights and phases come with the scene; the renderer raises the water from them Each rule only changes what the world already has: with no sun direction or celestial pole there is no day cycle, with no wind there are no gusts, and so on. The strips above are two minutes of examples/living-scene.yaml , with the day cycle switched on by its key. With seconds_per_day: 120 the sun goes round once. The wind swings around where it started and never quite repeats: it is a sum of three sines whose periods do not divide each other. The tide period is the 12.42 hours of the principal lunar semidiurnal tide (known as M2: high water twice a day, a little later each day), kept in proportion to the day, so 120 × 12.42 / 24 ≈ 62 seconds. The sun turns around the celestial pole, so it rises, climbs and sets along an arc; the rest of the day it is below the horizon. The clouds move with the wind, faster when it blows harder: at no wind at all they still creep, at 0.2 × speed , and at strength 1 they move at 1.2 × speed . Entities entity_motion moves the entities that ask for it in their properties. glTF node extras arrive as properties, so a scene can ask for motions without any code. Property Motion "bob": {"height": h, "period": s, "roll": radians} Floats up and down with a slight roll (a boat) "spin": {"axis": [x, y, z], "speed": radians per second} Turns around a local axis (a mill's sails) "path": {"points": [[x, y, z], …], "speed": units per second, "loop": true} Follows the points facing where it goes (+Z forward); without loop it turns around at the end An entity takes one motion: bob wins over spin, spin over path. Entities added later by other plugins start moving as soon as they appear: the rule reads entities with those properties. What each key is when it is left out: Motion Key When left out bob height 0.001 world units bob period 4 seconds bob roll 0.03 radians spin axis [0, 1, 0] , upright spin speed 1 radian per second path speed 1 world unit per second path loop true bob moves the entity up and down around where it rests and rolls it about its own X axis. The phase comes from where the entity is, so two buoys a little apart rise and fall out of step. spin turns the entity about an axis in its own frame, from where it rests. path places the entity on the route at a steady speed and turns it to face along the segment it is on. A loop goes back to the first point and starts over; without one, the entity comes back the same way. Where the entity rests is replaced by the route; its turn and scale are kept. Use cd ../go-simulator go run ./cmd/simulator -rules ../go-simulator-motion/examples/living-scene.yaml scene.glb examples/living-scene.yaml runs the plugin with go run ; after go install the command can be just [go-simulator-motion] . During development Go Simulator and Go Renderer are used from the folders next to this one ( replace in go.mod ). More in getting started .

the-quest.title: The motion quest
the-quest.text: The motion quest Make a still scene feel alive, one level at a time. Each level teaches one piece of the motion plugin and ends with something moving in the viewer. The quest map: a road from START through 5 levels — Timekeeper, Weatherman, Buoy keeper, Miller and Ferryman — to a final challenge, Harbour in motion We take the village of Go Scene Builder's quest (any .glb works) and make it move: the day passes, the wind gusts, a buoy bobs on the river, a weathervane turns and a boat sails a route. You write a tiny plugin of your own that puts the buoy, the vane and the boat in the world; the motion plugin moves them. Every level has the same shape: the idea (explained with something from everyday life), the rules , a checkpoint to know it works, and an optional bonus . Before you start You need Go 1.25 and GEOS ( sudo apt install libgeos-dev , brew install geos ). Clone the projects side by side and make a folder with a scene in it: git clone https://github.com/akrck02/go-renderer git clone https://github.com/akrck02/go-scene-builder git clone https://github.com/akrck02/go-simulator git clone https://github.com/akrck02/go-simulator-motion mkdir lively && cd lively cp ../village/village.glb . Everything here runs live , in Go Simulator's viewer: go run ../go-simulator/cmd/simulator -rules rules.yaml village.glb The motion rules belong on a realtime clock: they follow the seconds you watch, and the viewer's P (pause) and , . (slower, faster) apply to them. The animations below were made with the same rules on a stepped clock of half-second steps, captured with -advance . Level 1 · The Timekeeper Mission Pieces Time The day passes in two minutes day_cycle , a real-time stage, a toggle key 5 min The idea The sun does not move: the earth turns , and the sun seems to circle round the sky's pole. The day_cycle rule turns it round the pole once every seconds_per_day ; the renderer works out day, twilight and night from how high it is, and the stars and the moon follow. Build it rules.yaml : plugins: - name: motion command: [go, run, .] directory: ../go-simulator-motion stages: - name: harbour clock: realtime rules: - {rule: day_cycle, with: {seconds_per_day: 120}, toggle_key: T} Checkpoint The shadows turn, the light goes gold, the village falls into night and the sun comes up again, every two minutes. T stops the day where it is, and starts it again. Level 1: a day passing over the village, from noon to night Bonus (optional): a slow afternoon Achievement unlocked: Timekeeper Learn more: Motions: the environment Level 2 · The Weatherman Mission Pieces Time Wind that gusts, clouds that drift, a sea that rises and falls gusts , cloud_drift , tides 5 min The idea Real wind is never steady: it breathes , stronger and weaker, swinging a little either way. The gusts rule varies the wind the scene started with, as a sum of three slow waves that never quite repeat; plants made to sway bend with it, and cloud_drift moves the clouds along it. tides turns the tide's clock, about twice a day, if the scene has a tide. Each rule only changes what the scene already has: no wind in the scene, no gusts. Build it - {rule: gusts, with: {variation: 0.5, veering: 0.35}} - rule: cloud_drift - {rule: tides, with: {seconds_per_day: 120}, toggle_key: M} Checkpoint The garden's trees sway harder and softer; if the sky has clouds they drift with the wind. The village has no tide (its river has no tidal grid); a scene with one, such as Go Renderer's sample island, rises and falls, and M stops it. Bonus (optional): a storm Achievement unlocked: Weatherman Level 3 · The Buoy keeper Mission Pieces Time A buoy that bobs on the river entity_motion , bob , a plugin that adds things 10 min The idea The motion plugin moves things that ask to be moved : an entity with a bob property bobs, one with spin spins, one with path follows a route. It does not care who put the thing there: a node of the scene, or another plugin. It is like a dance teacher who teaches whoever comes to the class with a dance card. So we write the smallest plugin there is: it adds three things, each with its card, and does nothing else. Build it props/go.mod : module example.com/props go 1.25.6 require github.com/akrck02/go-simulator v0.0.0 replace ( github.com/akrck02/go-simulator => ../../go-simulator github.com/akrck02/go-renderer => ../../go-renderer github.com/akrck02/go-scene-builder => ../../go-scene-builder ) props/main.go : // Command props is a tiny plugin that puts things in the harbour for the motion plugin to move: a // buoy that bobs, a weathervane that spins and a boat on a route. It only adds them, once; motion // reads their properties and moves them. package main import ( "log" "github.com/akrck02/go-simulator/plugin" "github.com/akrck02/go-simulator/protocol" "github.com/akrck02/go-simulator/spatial" "github.com/akrck02/go-simulator/world" ) type props struct{} var propsRule = plugin.Definition{ Description: protocol.RuleDescription{ Name: "props", Summary: "Adds a buoy, a weathervane and a boat that ask the motion plugin to move them.", Writes: []string{"prop"}, Publishes: []protocol.OutputDescription{plugin.Kind("prop", "a thing that asks for a motion")}, }, New: func(plugin.Parameters) (plugin.Rule, error) { return &props{}, nil }, } func (rule *props) Start(context *plugin.Context) error { buoy := spatial.Translation(spatial.Vector{-0.02, 0.0115, 0.026}) context.Add(&world.Entity{Identifier: "buoy", Kind: "prop", Transform: &buoy, Shape: &world.Shape{Primitive: "box", Size: spatial.Vector{0.0015, 0.002, 0.0015}, Color: &[4]float32{0.9, 0.5, 0.1, 1}}, Properties: map[string]any{"label": "Buoy", "icon": "life-buoy", "bob": map[string]any{"height": 0.0006, "period": 3, "roll": 0.1}}}) vane := spatial.Translation(spatial.Vector{0.018, 0.028, -0.01}) context.Add(&world.Entity{Identifier: "vane", Kind: "prop", Transform: &vane, Shape: &world.Shape{Primitive: "box", Size: spatial.Vector{0.008, 0.0006, 0.0012}, Color: &[4]float32{0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 1}}, Properties: map[string]any{"label": "Weathervane", "icon": "wind", "spin": map[string]any{"axis": []any{0, 1, 0}, "speed": 1.5}}}) boat := spatial.Identity() context.Add(&world.Entity{Identifier: "boat", Kind: "prop", Transform: &boat, Shape: &world.Shape{Primitive: "box", Size: spatial.Vector{0.003, 0.0015, 0.007}, Color: &[4]float32{0.2, 0.35, 0.7, 1}}, Properties: map[string]any{"label": "Boat", "icon": "sailboat", "path": map[string]any{"points": []any{[]any{-0.05, 0.0115, 0.0295}, []any{0, 0.0115, 0.0215}, []any{0.05, 0.0115, 0.0315}}, "speed": 0.004, "loop": false}}}) return nil } func (rule *props) Step(*plugin.Context) error { return nil } func main() { log.SetFlags(0) harbour := &plugin.Plugin{Name: "props", Version: "0.1.0", Rules: []plugin.Definition{propsRule}} if err := harbour.Serve(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } } Positions are in the scene's kilometres, [x, y, z] , with z growing to the south. Then cd props && go mod tidy && cd .. , and in rules.yaml a second plugin and two rules: plugins: - {name: motion, command: [go, run, .], directory: ../go-simulator-motion} - {name: props, command: [go, run, .], directory: props} … - rule: props - rule: entity_motion Checkpoint An orange buoy on the river rises and falls every three seconds, rocking a little, with its label. (The vane and the boat move too: the next two levels are about them.) Level 3: the buoy bobbing on the river Bonus (optional): a row of buoys Add three more, a few metres apart. They bob out of step on their own: the phase comes from where each one is. Achievement unlocked: Buoy keeper Learn more: Motions: entities Level 4 · The Miller Mission Pieces Time A weathervane that turns spin 4 min The idea A mill's sails, a weathervane, a wheel: things that turn about an axis from where they rest. spin gives the axis in the thing's own frame ( [0, 1, 0] is upright) and the speed in radians a second (6.3 is a turn a second). Build it The vane in props/main.go already asks for it: "spin": map[string]any{"axis": []any{0, 1, 0}, "speed": 1.5} Checkpoint Over the high street, a dark bar turns about itself, a little more than a quarter turn a second. Level 4: the weathervane turning over the street Bonus (optional): a mill's sails Achievement unlocked: Miller Level 5 · The Ferryman Mission Pieces Time A boat that sails a route and comes back path , loop 4 min The idea A bus route : a list of stops, a speed, and either a loop (back to the first stop, round again) or there-and-back. path places the thing on the route at a steady speed, turned to face where it goes; "loop": false brings it back the way it came. Build it The boat in props/main.go : "path": map[string]any{"points": []any{[]any{-0.05, 0.0115, 0.0295}, []any{0, 0.0115, 0.0215}, []any{0.05, 0.0115, 0.0315}}, "speed": 0.004, "loop": false} 4 metres a second, along the river, under the bridge. Checkpoint The blue boat sails east along the river, under the bridge, and some 25 seconds later turns back. Level 5: the boat sailing along the river under the bridge Achievement unlocked: Ferryman Final challenge · Harbour in motion All of it at once in one real-time stage, and a key for each part: T the day, G the gusts, B the boats and buoys. Start with the day stopped, so the village opens in daylight. Hint: every rule takes a toggle_key , and enabled: false starts it switched off. Rare achievement unlocked: Harbour in motion Well done All six achievements: Timekeeper, Weatherman, Buoy keeper, Miller, Ferryman and Harbour in motion The village lives: its day turns, its wind breathes, and things you added move as they were asked. Ideas to keep going Idea Difficulty Hint Motions in the scene itself ⭐ glTF node extras become properties: "extras": {"bob": {…}} ( getting started ) A ferry that counts its trips ⭐⭐ Go Simulator's quest A town that grows while the day turns ⭐⭐⭐ A stepped stage with the urban plugin beside this real-time one Troubleshooting You see Why, and what to do Nothing moves The rule is off ( enabled: false , or its key pressed), or the stage is not realtime and has no pace The day does not change The scene has no sun direction: scenes from Go Scene Builder have one No gusts The scene starts with no wind: give it one in the scene's environment The buoy floats in the air or is buried Its height ( 0.0115 ) is in scene kilometres: move it a little up or down An entity bobs instead of following its path An entity takes one motion: bob wins over spin, spin over path ← All the documentation
